Longitudinal Summary

Over the periods from Q1 2019 through Q4 2019, the company consistently highlighted growth in vehicle deliveries and energy storage deployments, achieving quarterly records in both areas. Management emphasized ongoing investments in manufacturing capacity and customer infrastructure, including Gigafactory expansions and new product pipelines. However, no explicit forward guidance on customer growth metrics was provided, and the company disclosed risks related to meeting sales and delivery targets, as well as external factors such as government incentives. The filings also noted accounting considerations related to customer payments and resale value guarantees, but these did not directly quantify customer growth.

Forecasting Credibility: None

There are zero guidance/actual pairs available for customer growth, so it is not possible to assess management's forecasting credibility on this topic. Without explicit forward guidance and corresponding actual results, no pattern of met, exceeded, or missed expectations can be established. Therefore, the forecasting credibility rating must remain null.

  • Dependence on government incentives

Key Concerns

  • No direct forward guidance on customer growth metrics limits transparency on management's expectations and forecasting accuracy.
  • Accounting treatments related to customer payments and resale value guarantees may affect revenue recognition but do not clarify customer growth trends.
  • Risks disclosed about ramping business and infrastructure coverage suggest potential challenges in sustaining customer growth.

Conclusion

Customer growth is implied through record vehicle deliveries and energy storage deployments, supported by significant investments in manufacturing and infrastructure. However, the absence of explicit forward guidance and actual comparisons on customer growth metrics prevents a definitive assessment of management's forecasting ability in this area. The company acknowledges risks related to achieving sales and delivery targets and external factors such as changing government incentives, which could impact future customer growth. Overall, while operational indicators suggest growth, the lack of direct guidance and quantifiable customer growth data limits the ability to conclusively evaluate this topic.

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"Our plan to generate ongoing growth and demand, including by expanding and optimizing our vehicle service and charging operations and infrastructure, will require significant cash investments and management resources and may not meet 58 expectations with respect to additional sales, installations or servicing of our products or availability of public charging solutions."
  • jump to section"The ITC is currently scheduled to decline in phases, ultimately to 10% for commercial and utility systems and to 0% for customer-owned residential systems by January 2022."
  • jump to section"Our future growth and success is dependent upon consumers’ willingness to adopt electric vehicles and specifically our vehicles, especially in the mass market demographic which we are targeting with vehicles such as Model 3."
  • jump to section"If we experience any delays or cannot meet customer expectations in expanding our customer infrastructure network, or our expansion plans are not successful in continuing to grow demand, this could lead to a decrease or stagnation in sales or installations of our products and could negatively impact our business, prospects, financial condition and operating results."
  • jump to section"The leasing program also relies on our ability to secure adequate financing and/or business partners to fund and grow this program, and screen for and manage customer credit risk."
  • jump to section"We plan to generate ongoing growth and demand, including by globally expanding and optimizing our vehicle service and charging operations and infrastructure."

MD&A
  • jump to section"Automotive—Deliveries and Customer Infrastructure In the third quarter of 2019, we achieved a new quarterly record for total vehicles delivered."
  • jump to section"39 We remain focused on growth for our energy storage products, and achieved a new quarterly deployment record in the third quarter of 2019."
  • jump to section"Considering the pipeline of new products planned at this point, and all other infrastructure growth and investments in Gigafactory 1, Gigafactory 2, Gigafactory Shanghai and future planned manufacturing facilities, we currently estimate that capital expenditures will be between $2.0 to $2.5 billion annually for the next two fiscal years."
  • jump to section"However, if our customer vehicles, particularly in the rapidly growing Model 3 fleet, experience unexpected reliability issues, it could outpace and overburden our servicing capabilities and parts inventory."
  • jump to section"After reestablishing certain production at Gigafactory 1 for our energy storage products in 2019 to reduce backlog and shorten customer wait times, we are now focused on further manufacturing efficiencies and improvements in our installation processes as we ramp."
  • jump to section"Summary of Cash Flows Nine Months Ended September 30, (Dollars in millions) 2019 2018 Net cash provided by operating activities $ 980 $ 863 Net cash used in investing activities $ (1,033 ) $ (1,972 ) Net cash provided by financing activities $ 1,608 $ 686 49 Cash Flows from Operating Activities Our cash flows from operating activities are significantly affected by our cash investments to support the growth of our business in areas such as research and development and selling, general and administrative and working capital, especially inventory, which includes vehicles in transit."

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"60 Our plan to generate ongoing growth and demand, including by expanding and optimizing our vehicle service and charging operations and infrastructure, will require significant cash investments and management resources and may not meet expectations with respect to additional sales, installations or servicing of our products or availability of public charging solutions."
  • jump to section"The ITC is currently scheduled to decline in phases, ultimately to 10% for commercial and utility systems and to 0% for customer-owned residential systems by January 2022."
  • jump to section"Our future growth and success is dependent upon consumers’ willingness to adopt electric vehicles and specifically our vehicles, especially in the mass market demographic which we are targeting with vehicles such as Model 3."
  • jump to section"If we experience any delays or cannot meet customer expectations in expanding our customer infrastructure network, or our expansion plans are not successful in continuing to grow demand, this could lead to a decrease or stagnation in sales or installations of our products and could negatively impact our business, prospects, financial condition and operating results."
  • jump to section"The leasing program also relies on our ability to secure adequate financing and/or business partners to fund and grow this program, and screen for and manage customer credit risk."
  • jump to section"We plan to generate ongoing growth and demand, including by globally expanding and optimizing our vehicle service and charging operations and infrastructure."

  • jump to section"As discussed in and subject to the considerations referenced in Part II, Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Management Opportunities, Challenges and Risks and 2020 Outlook—Trends in Cash Flow, Capital Expenditures and Operating Expenses in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, considering the expected pace of the manufacturing ramps for our products, construction and expansion of our factories, and pipeline of projects under development, and consistent with our current strategy of using a partner to manufacture battery cells, as well as considering all other infrastructure growth, we currently expect our average annual capital expenditures in 2020 and the two succeeding fiscal years to be $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion."

  • jump to section"Energy Generation and Storage We revamped key aspects of our solar operations in 2019 by streamlining traditionally complex ordering, permitting, installation and back-end service processes to enhance the customer experience, especially for retrofit solar installations."
